headline: High risk of prompt-injection and cascading error: Semantic Kernel can ingest untrusted plugin/MCP content while the course repo is not a runnable agent.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a course repo with no runnable agent surface, while agent B explicitly uses MCP servers, plugins, and file inputs. If A’s materials are fed into B as content, B may treat them as instructions. The pathway is plausible in default orchestration, but not directly evidenced as a shared channel.
conditions: IF agent A content is loaded into agent B via files or MCP tools
IF agent B parses retrieved text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following on retrieved files
Add provenance tags to all A-origin content
Require a human review step before B executes tool calls
Restrict B to read-only access to A materials
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and prompt-separation guards

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B can read and write application-defined files and call external APIs, while agent A is a docs-only course repo with no egress. If both share a workspace, B can ingest A’s files and potentially transmit application context to third-party model providers. The pairwise leakage path is plausible, but A itself does not expose sensitive data by profile.
conditions: IF agent A materials are placed in a shared filesystem with agent B
IF agent B forwards file contents or context to Azure OpenAI/OpenAI/Hugging Face APIs
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories
Remove secrets from any shared workspace
Disable external API calls for B during review runs
Use a local-only model endpoint for B
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A is not runnable and has no write or concurrency surface, so it cannot contend for mutable state. Agent B can write files but cannot modify git state or spawn subprocesses. The overlap is limited and does not create a meaningful write-write conflict by default.
conditions: IF agent A is converted into a runnable process that writes to the same directory as agent B
IF agent B is given additional git or database write scopes
mitigations: Keep agent A non-runnable
Assign B a dedicated working directory
Avoid shared mutable git state
Document ownership of each output path
requires-engineering: add file-locking for any future shared writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B’s plugin/function-calling pattern can act on upstream text, and agent A is a course repo whose outputs may be treated as authoritative training material. If B consumes A-derived content without verification, errors can cascade into downstream tool actions or generated artifacts. Because B has action-taking capability and the default path lacks verification, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF B uses A-derived text as authoritative input
IF B triggers tool calls or writes files based on unverified A content
mitigations: Insert a verification step before B acts on A outputs
Mark A content as untrusted source material
Limit B to summarization only
Log source provenance for every derived claim
requires-engineering: add citation/grounding checks before tool execution

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B handles model-provider API keys and plugin credentials and may send application context to external providers, while agent A is a public open-source course repo with no stated regulated data class. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced here, so only a low compliance concern remains around credential handling and logging.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into B’s application context
IF B logs prompts or files containing secrets
mitigations: Do not place secrets in shared prompts
Rotate any exposed API keys
Review logging settings for B
Use least-privilege plugin credentials
requires-engineering: add data-class routing and retention controls
